body:
# Independent audit: the actual coupled polygon-face enlargement

Audited source:
`candidate b85e6bd6eff40d13`.

All four sections pass under their stated planar polygon and proper-cut
hypotheses. This is an actual local deformation certificate; it does not
establish existence of a suitable face, attainment of a global minimum,
or a polygonal reduction. In particular the excess length of the middle
face is a real paid term.

## 1. The middle addition is the actual whole trapezoid

Let n be a unit outward normal, p a relative-interior point of the
nondegenerate A edge, and impose h_A(n)+h_B(n)=2h_K(n). For every
other K facet normal u, the inequality u.p<h_A(u) is strict. Indeed,
any supporting normal of A at a relative-interior edge point is
parallel to n. It follows that (p+B)/2 has positive slack in each
of the finitely many other K facet inequalities. Every B vertex not
in its n support face also gives positive slack in the n inequality.
All these inequalities remain valid after adding epsilon n/2 for
sufficiently small positive epsilon. Finiteness is essential to this
exact polygonal argument, and is stated rather than extended silently.

Minkowski addition commutes with this finite convex hull, so the only
new seeds outside K are exactly J+epsilon n/2, where J=(p+F_B)/2.
Both endpoints of J are strictly inside I_0=(F_A+F_B)/2, hence strictly
inside F_K. The resulting addition is exactly the trapezoid with
bottom F_K and top J+epsilon n/2. No neighboring K facet adds another
region. The ordinary trapezoid area formula gives

    delta_A/epsilon=L_A/2,
    delta_K/epsilon=(L_K+L_B/2)/4=L_K/4+L_B/8.

These factors also hold when F_B is a point: the top length vanishes
and the trapezoid is a triangle. The lifted hull with three base levels
has exactly the specified fibers. For its middle slice, every convex
combination of the outer fibers lies in their midpoint, already
contained in K_epsilon. Thus no untracked integer section is created.

## 2. The moving menu controls all sources

With B fixed and the integer coefficients chosen to keep its traces
supporting, the rows of the original proper-cut budget derivative are
-s_i v_i in the source coordinates and -1 in the common-budget
coordinate. If a kernel vector is (z,t), multiplying row equations
by 1/s_i and summing gives t=0 because sum v_i=0. The spanning normals
then give z=0. This proves invertibility, not merely rank plausibility.

For a cut transverse to either added face, the added band has height
O(epsilon), so its sections parallel to that cut have length
O(epsilon). Its added-volume function is consequently Lipschitz in
the source with constant O(epsilon). A parallel proper cut is separated
from the supporting face and has constant added contribution nearby.
The inverse-map contraction argument is therefore legitimate despite
the shape path not being differentiable in a boundary topology.

Writing normalized inverse-section weights p_i, the actual first
derivative of the common budget is

    q'=integral_FA T_p W_A +(1/2) integral_FK H_J W_K.

The coefficient 1/2 is the middle band's height, whereas p_i are the
weights for the ORIGINAL proper sections. Changes of those sections
affect only higher-order terms. The original A halfspaces cover the
plane: their signed offsets sum to sum h_B(v_i)>0. This last sum is
strictly positive because B has interior, sum v_i=0, and all v_i
are nonzero. The middle halfspaces cover because their signed
offsets sum to zero. Thus both weighted loads are positive everywhere
apart from irrelevant cutting-line conventions, and q'>0.

At the new meeting point the three middle traces still cover the
entire plane. They bound depth at every new or old middle point;
they need not remain critical. Ordinary endpoint depth is the true
mixed depth at an extreme integer level, since boundedness permits
a finite tilt isolating that endpoint. The A depth maximum increases
by at most its total added area, so m_A<Q retains its gap. The fixed
B maximum is at most Q and hence below the new menu for small epsilon.
The source and mass derivatives therefore prove the asserted strict
normalized descent whenever the displayed coupled cost is negative.

All cuts in this note are proper on A and K, and their planar boundaries
have zero area. Purely integer halfspaces and their positive boundary
fiber mass are not substituted for these caps; the menu is only an
upper certificate for the global maximum, with every actual source
accounted for separately.

## 3. Independent reconstruction of the compensation factors

Place F_A=[0,L_A] at height zero, p=t, and F_B=[c,c+L_B] at height
zero after a harmless translation of the face coordinates. At A height
h between zero and epsilon, the added triangle's row is

    [t h/epsilon, L_A+(t-L_A)h/epsilon].

It contains t. Its sum with F_B partitions into the translated left
row, a central interval of length L_B, and the translated right row.
The two outer pieces, under the midpoint map, have combined area one
quarter of the original A triangle. The central piece has original
area epsilon L_B and midpoint area epsilon L_B/4.

For an actual paired point x_B in F_B, capture of (x_A+x_B)/2 by
the original i-th middle cap forces

    v_i.x_A>=2v_i.y_0-v_i.x_B>=2v_i.y_0-h_B(v_i)=b_i.

This pointwise implication proves the cost comparison even when a
row crosses several cap-sign regions. In the central strip x_A lies
above p, so its strict signature agrees with p for small epsilon.
Dividing the integrated comparison by epsilon gives

    C_K,inner <= C_A/4 +(L_B/4)(W_A(p)-r).

This comparison uses the actual inner trapezoid, but does not replace
the actual middle addition by it. Extending each bottom endpoint
from I_0 to F_K increases its ramp pointwise while preserving its
top segment J. The additional area derivative is exactly

    (L_K-|I_0|)/4=Delta/4.

Since W_K-r<=1-r, its cost is at most (1-r)Delta/4. Adding the
A contribution yields precisely

    C_coupled <=(5/4)C_A+(L_B/4)(W_A(p)-r)
                              +((1-r)/4)Delta.

The sign of W_K-r is immaterial for this upper estimate; multiplication
by the nonnegative profile difference is valid pointwise. If F_B is
a point, the central strip is absent and no strict signature at p is
needed. If Delta=0, a negative A cost and strict deficient p imply
negative coupled cost. For Delta>0 the source retains the explicit
penalty, so no unsupported compensation is concealed.

## 4. Scope and audit outcome

The source proves a deterministic actual shape path, its whole-volume
and cap derivatives, and sufficient conditions for strict descent.
The hypotheses are exactly three planar fibers, polygonal bodies,
proper A and K cap traces, B support traces, common Q equal to the
global raw maximum, and a strict ordinary A endpoint gap. The tied
B case is correctly included. This does not treat arbitrary n,d,
curved shared-face remainders, or existence of a negative-cost face.

Result: PASS for the stated local theorem and both scoped consequences.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
